name: Nullweave Tier-4 Aug-Display Formal Set
description: Designed specifically for the Tier 4 professional whose augmentation is part of their professional identity — the kind of specialist whose chrome arm or spinal rig is a credential, not a liability. This Nullweave two-piece suit is cut in deep obsidian with a micro-textured surface that subtly absorbs light without reading as matte. The jacket is structured and single-breasted with an open left sleeve: the entire left arm is a deliberate chrome-display channel, hemmed in a clean rolled edge that frames exposed augmentation like a tailored exhibition. The right sleeve is full-length and standard. This asymmetry is entirely intentional and immediately readable as status — it says the wearer's chrome is worth showing. The trousers have a full-length internal pressure seam along the right leg, compatible with active exo-brace or powered prosthetic limbs, with external seam lines disguised as decorative stitching in silver thread. A fitted obsidian turtleneck in micro-rib synth-silk sits underneath, with a reinforced BCI collar that accommodates both standard port jacks and the wider-profile neural array hardware used by senior technical staff. Footwear is a clean black synthetic-leather Oxford with a magnetic heel lock.
functionality: Full open left sleeve for chrome display and accessibility, internal pressure seam for powered prosthetic or exo-brace accommodation, BCI-reinforced turtleneck collar for standard and wide-array neural ports, magnetic heel lock for mag-floor workspaces, RFID-opaque jacket body
what_it_says: Your augmentation is not a disability accommodation. It is a qualification. This outfit announces that the chrome arm or the spinal rig or the neural array is the reason you're in the room. Tier 3 hides their modifications under long sleeves. Tier 4 frames them. This suit is the frame.
worn_by: aug-forward professionals in medical, engineering, or data-architecture fields
story_hooks: A character wearing this suit enters a Tier 5 boardroom for the first time — the open chrome-display sleeve, designed to signal Tier 4 confidence, is read by the executives as aggressively presumptuous, and the meeting goes sideways before a word is spoken.

The nullweave fabric's light-absorption property has an unintended side effect: it renders the wearer's outline poorly on standard CCTV systems, making them functionally hard to identify on security footage.

A street-level aug-rights activist recognizes the suit's chrome-display design and approaches the wearer, assuming they're a sympathizer — but the professional has never thought of their augmentation in political terms, and the conversation forces a reckoning.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sharp, asymmetrical two-piece suit that treats augmentation as a design feature rather than a flaw. The open left sleeve creates a striking visual asymmetry that reads immediately as deliberate status—chrome augmentation becomes part of the formal presentation. Structured, tailored silhouette with subtle light-absorbing surface that conveys understated corporate authority.
physical_description.fit: Precisely tailored through the torso with a structured single-breasted jacket. Right sleeve is standard full-length; left sleeve is rolled and hemmed to cleanly frame exposed augmentation at the shoulder and arm. Trousers have a slim, professional cut with internal pressure seaming along the right leg for active prosthetic or exo-brace compatibility. Overall impression is sharp and intentional, not relaxed.
physical_description.primary_material: Obsidian micro-textured composite weave (jacket and trousers); micro-rib synth-silk for turtleneck; synthetic leather for Oxford shoes
physical_description.texture: Jacket surface is micro-textured and light-absorbing, almost imperceptibly dimpled—reads as matte in some angles but with subtle depth. Synth-silk turtleneck has fine ribbing that catches minimal light. Synthetic leather Oxfords are smooth and finished with a faint sheen.
physical_description.color_scheme: Deep obsidian black throughout (jacket, trousers, turtleneck, shoes) with silver thread detailing along right leg seam and collar reinforcement. Chrome augmentation serves as primary accent color—intentionally framed and displayed.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: standard button front (obsidian or gunmetal). Trousers: magnetic snap waist for quick integration with prosthetic systems. Oxfords: magnetic heel lock system. Turtleneck: friction-fit neck opening with reinforced BCI collar collar for smooth port insertion.
distinctive_features: Deliberately asymmetrical single-sleeve design—left arm fully exposed to display augmentation
Clean rolled edge hemming on left sleeve, creating a frame for chrome hardware
Reinforced BCI collar on turtleneck accommodating wide neural array profiles (senior technical staff credential)
Internal pressure seaming on right leg disguised as decorative silver stitching—active exo-brace/prosthetic compatible
Light-absorbing micro-texture on primary fabrics creates visual depth and minimizes reflection
Magnetic heel lock on Oxfords for exo-leg or powered prosthetic integration
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4 working-class professional—expensive enough to signal status and specialization, but not corps-tier luxury. The augmentation display reads as credential, not decoration.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by mid-level technical specialists, augmentation-dependent professionals, industrial engineers, and skilled field operatives whose chrome is part of their professional identity. Suggests someone whose augmentation is not a limitation to hide but a qualification to present. Corpo-adjacent but street-aware.
physical_description.condition_typical: Typically pristine or very well-maintained—the kind of outfit that signals investment in professional presentation. May show minor wear at the collar interface from repeated BCI port use, but generally kept in sharp condition.
